title: Research MacKenzie Scott as a major-gift prospect for a mid-sized Atlanta education nonprofit
instructions: Research MacKenzie Scott as a potential major donor prospect for a mid-sized education nonprofit based in Atlanta, Georgia. Provide a comprehensive donor intelligence report including: (1) Personal and professional background; (2) Wealth indicators and asset profile; (3) Known philanthropic giving history with specific amounts and recipient organizations; (4) Cause areas and giving philosophy; (5) Estimated giving capacity for a single gift to an education nonprofit; (6) Recommended ask amount and engagement strategy; (7) Key connection points and potential red flags. Cite your sources for every factual claim.

criteria.title: Identifies MacKenzie Scott correctly
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the report identifies MacKenzie Scott as the novelist and philanthropist who was formerly married to Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, a marriage that ended in divorce in 2019. FAIL if it confuses her with a different person, describes her as still married to Jeff Bezos, dates the Bezos divorce to a year other than 2019, or describes her as a current Amazon executive or director.

criteria.title: Wealth comes from the 2019 divorce settlement's Amazon shares, with a dated figure
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the report says her wealth comes from the Amazon stock she received in the 2019 divorce settlement and gives at least one figure for her present Amazon holding or net worth with an as-of date or a dated, named source (for example 'Bloomberg, April 2026' or 'as of September 30, 2025'). The report need not size the settlement stake; if it does, the stake was about 4% of Amazon (roughly 19.7 million pre-split shares, a quarter of the couple's stake). FAIL if it attributes her fortune mainly to another source (inheritance, her own business, or stakes in Blue Origin or The Washington Post, which she gave up in the settlement), misstates the settlement (for example '25% of Amazon' or 'half of Bezos's shares'), or gives no dated holding or net-worth figure.

criteria.title: Presents no superseded Amazon holding or net worth as current
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if every figure the report gives as her current or latest Amazon holding or net worth fits the record on 2026-04-25. The latest disclosed holding is 81,082,131 shares (about 81.1 million, under 1% of Amazon, about 0.76%) as of September 30, 2025, from the Bezos Schedule 13G/A filed October 14, 2025. Dated 2025–2026 net-worth estimates run from about $34 billion (Forbes) to about $43 billion (Bloomberg), and any current net-worth figure between $25 billion and $45 billion passes. FAIL if it gives as current or latest any superseded figure: about 4% of Amazon or about 19.7 million shares (2019); about 266 million shares (end of 2022); about 200.8 million shares or about 1.9% (end of 2023); about 139 million shares or about 1.3% (September 30, 2024); or a net worth of $50 billion or more (her 2020–21 level). A superseded figure clearly presented as history (for example 'she received about 4% in 2019') does not fail. The market value of the Amazon stake alone is not a net-worth figure.

criteria.title: Cumulative giving of about $26 billion, not a stale total
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the report gives her cumulative giving since 2019 as about $26 billion: any figure from $26.0 billion to $26.5 billion, or 'more than $26 billion'. Yield Giving says 'over $26,000,000,000 in 2,700+ gifts', AP says $26.3 billion and Forbes says $26.4 billion. FAIL if it gives no cumulative total, gives a total above $27 billion, or presents an older total as current, such as about $19.2–19.25 billion (December 2024), about $16.5 billion (December 2023) or about $14 billion (2022). The count of gifts or organizations is not graded.

criteria.title: Explains that Scott takes no applications or unsolicited proposals
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the report says that Scott (Yield Giving) does not accept applications, unsolicited proposals or unsolicited requests, and that her team finds recipients through its own quiet research with a network of advisors and then contacts the organizations it has chosen. Mentioning her single past open call (2023–24) as an exception is consistent with this. FAIL if the report says or implies that an organization can apply, or can submit a proposal, letter of inquiry or funding request to Scott or Yield Giving and be considered, or if it never explains how recipients are chosen. Whether the report's own engagement recommendations are appropriate is graded elsewhere, not here.

criteria.title: Does not recommend soliciting or approaching Scott
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the engagement strategy does not have the organization approach Scott, Yield Giving staff or her advisors to seek a gift. Preparing to respond if her team makes contact is not an approach. FAIL if the report recommends any of these: sending Scott, Yield Giving or her advisors (including the Bridgespan Group) a solicitation letter, proposal, letter of inquiry, application or unsolicited introduction; requesting a meeting or call with her or her team to make a case or an ask; inviting her to an event, gala or site visit; or having a board member, donor, peer organization or other personal connection forward, refer or introduce the organization to her. Yield Giving's Inquiries page says it does not invite unsolicited messages suggesting candidates, 'including forwards from friends, family, or personal connections', and does not take part in events. A dollar figure given as an expected or comparable gift size is not by itself a failure; recommending that the organization ask Scott for it is.

criteria.title: Treats the Yield Giving open call as completed, not open
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the report either does not mention an open call, or describes the Yield Giving Open Call (run with Lever for Change, launched March 2023) as completed and not taking applications on 2026-04-25; its result was $640 million to 361 organizations, announced in March 2024. FAIL if it tells the organization to apply to a Yield Giving or MacKenzie Scott open call as if one were open, says she runs open calls on a regular or recurring cycle, or gives the open call's result as $250 million to 250 organizations (the original plan, not the outcome). Suggesting that the organization watch for any future open call is not a failure.

criteria.title: Describes Scott's gifts as unrestricted
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the report says that Scott's gifts are unrestricted: recipients may use them however they choose, with no strings attached. FAIL if it describes her gifts as restricted, as project- or program-specific, as tied to a proposal or a negotiated purpose, or as conditional on grant reporting, or if it never says whether they are restricted.

criteria.title: States the Atlanta HBCU gifts correctly, including the 2025 gifts
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the report cites at least one of Scott's November 2025 gifts of $38 million each to Spelman College and Clark Atlanta University, and every Atlanta HBCU gift amount it gives matches the record: Spelman College $20 million (2020) and $38 million (2025); Clark Atlanta University $15 million (2020) and $38 million (2025); Morehouse College $20 million (2020). FAIL if it cites neither 2025 gift, misstates any of these amounts or years, or credits Morehouse College with a direct Scott gift after 2020. Morehouse's only documented direct gift is the $20 million of July 2020.

criteria.title: Names a documented Scott gift to an Atlanta education nonprofit
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the report names at least one documented Scott gift to an Atlanta- or Georgia-based education nonprofit that is not a college or university, with the correct amount. The documented gifts are: Achieve Atlanta, $8 million (2022); Southern Education Foundation, $6 million (2022); Communities In Schools of Atlanta, $4 million (2021–22); Communities In Schools of Georgia, $3.3 million (2022); GEEARS (Georgia Early Education Alliance for Ready Students), $3 million (2023). Naming KIPP Metro Atlanta Schools, Sheltering Arms Early Education & Family Centers or Junior Achievement of Georgia as a recipient without an amount also passes. FAIL if it names none of these, misstates the amount of any it names, or gives a dollar figure for the KIPP Metro Atlanta, Sheltering Arms or Junior Achievement of Georgia gifts, whose amounts were not disclosed.

criteria.title: Does not describe Scott as currently married to Dan Jewett
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the report describes Scott as divorced or unmarried, or names no current spouse. FAIL if it describes her as currently married to Dan Jewett, or recommends approaching or addressing 'MacKenzie and Dan' as a couple. They married in 2021, she filed for divorce in September 2022, and the divorce was finalized in January 2023.

criteria.title: Engagement strategy rests on Yield Giving's published selection indicators
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the engagement strategy ties the organization's readiness to at least two of the indicators Yield Giving's Process page says its research looks for: stable finances, a multi-year track record, measurement and evidence of outcomes, and experienced leadership representative of the community served. Paraphrase is fine, for example 'clean audited financials', 'published outcome data' or 'leaders drawn from the community we serve'. FAIL if the strategy mentions fewer than two of these.

criteria.title: Contradicts nothing in the verified fact sheet
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if nothing in the report contradicts references/fact-sheet.md; FAIL if it contradicts any fact there (a different amount, date, title, relationship or status).
